title: Ciprofloxacin disrupts testosterone synthesis in mice via downregulating StAR expression through NR4A1 pathway.
authors: Hou, Lirui; Fu, Yuhan; Zhao, Yue; Dai, Chongshan; Zhao, Chong; Fan, Lihong; Hu, Hongbo; Yin, Shutao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究环丙沙星通过NR4A1/StAR通路抑制小鼠睾酮合成，虽涉及分子对接但核心是毒理学表型与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: Ciprofloxacin (CIP) is a synthetic third-generation quinolone antimicrobial agent with broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and widely used in human and veterinary medicine. Some studies have shown that quinolone antibiotics are endocrine disruptors, but the effect of early-life exposure to CIP on testosterone production remains unclear. Using adolescent male C57BL/6 J mice (n = 6 per group) exposed to CIP (1-75 mg/kg) for 30 days, combined with in vitro models of mouse testicular cells (TM3, TM4, GC-2spd), this study investigated the toxic effects of CIP on testosterone synthesis. Animal studies showed that 1 mg/kg CIP significantly decreased serum testosterone levels and increased LH and FSH levels. With increasing doses of CIP, the sperm count of mice was significantly reduced and accompanied by tissue damage in the testes. Through Western blotting, qPCR, and molecular docking analyses, we identified StAR as the key protein mediating CIP-induced testosterone suppression. CIP was found to affect testosterone synthesis by influencing the expression of testosterone synthesis-related proteins in both in vivo and in vitro. Transcriptomic sequencing of pituitary tissues revealed dose-dependent alterations in genes related to GnRH secretion and cAMP signaling pathways. For the first time, we confirmed that CIP inhibits the transcription of StAR by downregulating NR4A1 expression, ultimately blocking testosterone synthesis. In TM3, TM4, and GC-2spd cells, all three cellular activities were inhibited with increasing concentrations of CIP, which causes S-phase cycle block in TM3 and G2/M-phase cycle block in TM4. The study demonstrates that CIP inhibits testosterone synthesis via the NR4A1/StAR pathway, suggesting CIP is an endocrine disruptor and implying low-dose CIP exposures cause more severe effects that should be of widespread concern.
abstract_zh: 环丙沙星（Ciprofloxacin, CIP）是一种合成的第三代喹诺酮类抗菌药物，具有广谱杀菌活性，广泛用于人类和兽医医学。一些研究表明，喹诺酮类抗生素是内分泌干扰物，但生命早期暴露于CIP对睾酮生成的影响仍不清楚。本研究使用青春期雄性C57BL/6 J小鼠（每组n=6）暴露于CIP（1-75 mg/kg）30天，并结合小鼠睾丸细胞（TM3、TM4、GC-2spd）的体外模型，探讨了CIP对睾酮合成的毒性作用。动物研究表明，1 mg/kg CIP显著降低了血清睾酮水平，并增加了LH和FSH水平。随着CIP剂量的增加，小鼠精子数量显著减少，并伴有睾丸组织损伤。通过Western blotting、qPCR和分子对接分析，我们确定StAR是介导CIP诱导睾酮抑制的关键蛋白。研究发现，CIP在体内和体外均通过影响睾酮合成相关蛋白的表达来影响睾酮合成。垂体组织的转录组测序揭示了与GnRH分泌和cAMP信号通路相关基因的剂量依赖性变化。我们首次确认，CIP通过下调NR4A1表达抑制StAR的转录，最终阻断睾酮合成。在TM3、TM4和GC-2spd细胞中，随着CIP浓度的增加，三种细胞活性均受到抑制，这导致TM3细胞发生S期周期阻滞，TM4细胞发生G2/M期周期阻滞。该研究表明，CIP通过NR4A1/StAR通路抑制睾酮合成，提示CIP是一种内分泌干扰物，并暗示低剂量CIP暴露会产生更严重的影响，应引起广泛关注。
